title: Banach–Steinhaus from Baire — Goal and Plan
content: The docstring fixes the objective: derive the Uniform Boundedness Principle (Banach–Steinhaus) directly from the gallery Baire category theorem (BaireCategoryTheoremOQ01.baire_nonempty_interior), NOT by invoking Mathlib's packaged banach_steinhaus. It previews the classical textbook argument — closed sublevel sets, their union exhausting the space, Baire producing a ball of local uniform boundedness, and a shell estimate promoting that to a uniform operator-norm bound — and notes this is genuinely distinct from Mathlib's current proof, which goes through the barrelled-space / equicontinuity framework. Three results: the principle, an equicontinuity-form restatement, and the contrapositive resonance principle.
mathContext: If $\{g_i\}$ are bounded operators on a Banach space with $\sup_i \|g_i x\| < \infty$ for each $x$, then $\sup_i \|g_i\| < \infty$.

title: The Uniform Boundedness Principle
content: uniform_boundedness is the heart of the entry. Define the sublevel sets e n = ⋂ i, {x | ‖g i x‖ ≤ n}; each is closed because x ↦ ‖g i x‖ is continuous (isClosed_le applied to the intersection). Pointwise boundedness — every x has a finite bound C, dominated by some natural m — gives ⋃ n e n = univ. Completeness makes E a Baire space, so the gallery category form baire_nonempty_interior returns an m with interior (e m) nonempty: a ball ball x ε on which every ‖g i ·‖ ≤ m. The off-center bound is homogenized by the shell trick (see the dedicated annotation), and ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_of_shell converts the resulting proportional bound into ‖g i‖ ≤ 2m/(ε/‖c‖), a bound independent of i.
mathContext: Baire gives a ball where all $\|g_i\cdot\| \le m$; the shell estimate then yields $\|g_i\| \le 2m/(\varepsilon/\|c\|)$, uniform in $i$.

title: The Shell Trick: Local Bound ⇒ Operator-Norm Bound
content: Baire only hands back a ball ball x ε around an *unknown, off-center* point x; turning that into an operator-norm bound (which is about behavior near 0) is the crux. The device: for y in the shell ε/‖c‖ ≤ ‖y‖ < ε, both y+x and x lie in the ball, so linearity gives g i y = g i (y+x) − g i x and the triangle inequality gives ‖g i y‖ ≤ m + m = 2m — a *flat* bound. The lower shell bound ε/‖c‖ ≤ ‖y‖ then upgrades the flat 2m into the *proportional* 2m ≤ (2m/(ε/‖c‖))·‖y‖, exactly the hypothesis ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_of_shell needs. The unknown center x is absorbed into the harmless factor of 2; the nontrivially-normed-field scalar c (with ‖c‖ > 1, from NormedField.exists_one_lt_norm) supplies the shell's inner radius.
mathContext: $g_i y = g_i(y+x) - g_i x \Rightarrow \|g_i y\| \le 2m$; with $\varepsilon/\|c\| \le \|y\|$, $\;2m \le \frac{2m}{\varepsilon/\|c\|}\,\|y\|$, so $\|g_i\| \le \frac{2m}{\varepsilon/\|c\|}$.

title: Equicontinuity Form: a Single Constant C'
content: uniform_boundedness_with_const repackages the uniform operator-norm bound as a single nonnegative constant C' with ‖g i x‖ ≤ C'·‖x‖ for every operator i and every point x. It is obtained by chaining le_opNorm (‖g i x‖ ≤ ‖g i‖·‖x‖) with the uniform bound on ‖g i‖, taking max C' 0 to guarantee nonnegativity. This homogeneous (equicontinuity) inequality — not the bare operator-norm bound — is the form actually used in convergence-of-operators arguments and in proving that a pointwise limit of bounded operators is bounded.
mathContext: $\exists C' \ge 0,\ \forall i\,\forall x,\ \|g_i x\| \le C'\|x\|$ — uniform equicontinuity of the family at the origin.

title: Resonance: the Contrapositive and Its Applications
content: exists_resonance_of_not_uniformly_bounded is the contrapositive (Banach–Steinhaus's original 'condensation of singularities' form): if the operator norms are NOT uniformly bounded, then the pointwise-boundedness hypothesis must fail somewhere — there is a single point x of *resonance* at which no finite C bounds ‖g i x‖ over all i (sup_i ‖g i x‖ = ∞). The Lean proof is a clean by_contra / push_neg reduction back to uniform_boundedness. This is the genuinely useful form in applications: rather than constructing a singular object by hand, one shows the relevant operators are not uniformly bounded and lets resonance produce the witness — the mechanism behind the existence of a continuous function whose Fourier series diverges at a point (the partial-sum operators are unbounded in operator norm).
mathContext: $\neg(\exists C',\forall i,\ \|g_i\| \le C') \Rightarrow \exists x,\ \neg\exists C,\forall i,\ \|g_i x\| \le C$ — a single point of simultaneous blow-up.
